title: R-GCN basis coefficients factorized by relation attributes
hypothesis: A shared R-GCN basis plus a learned mapping from relation attributes to basis coefficients composes unseen attribute combinations with fewer bytes and better operator quality than free per-relation R-GCN coefficients, and beats a native attribute-conditioned coefficient generator.
mirror_coordinate: four-value attribute feature code and learned code-to-basis map
logical_multiplicity: 32 relations spanning eight attribute combinations, including two held-out types
controls: free R-GCN basis coefficients per seen relation

development.selection_metric: held-out operator nRMSE / relation ranking and actual complete bytes

fresh.reason: no audit after exact native attribute-generator alias

storage.authority: actual serialized full inference payload bytes

success_gate: Held-out operator nRMSE <=.02 and Hits@1 within two points of independent; >=25% complete byte savings vs free R-GCN coefficients; strict quality/byte improvement over native attribute generator.
failure_gate: quality/storage miss or exact native attribute-generator function/payload alias is FAIL for Mirror-specific value.
boundaries: Relation attributes are explicit and all attribute tables are charged.
No trained R-GCN or real knowledge graph claim.
